Name: Franklin Veaux
Question: How do people move on so quickly? I’m still sprung over someone I was dating and he found someone else so fast. I feel hurt because I’m still head over heels over him while he’s out enjoying his life with someone new
Answer: Okay, so I’m not sure how well this generalizes, but something I’ve noticed about people who recover quickly from the end of a relationship vs those who don’t is that the people who recover quickly tend, in my experience and observation, to be people who have high self-efficacy and self-sufficiency, whereas those who don’t, tend to be lower in self-efficacy, self-sufficiency, or both. Now, I freely admit that I am extrapolating from a limited sample set, and it could also be some combination of selection bias and confirmation bias at work, but I’ve noticed very strong correlations between “starts dating again soon” and “believes in one’s own ability to thrive.” Self-efficacy, put very simply, is the idea that you can do what you put your mind to—that you have the skills and tools you need to be successful at what you want to do. Self-sufficiency is the belief that you are enough—that you are worthy, that you have value, that you are an independent autonomous being who can be happy on your own. If you believe you are not worthy, or that you cannot succeed on your own, or that you cannot be happy on your own—that is, you believe that reliance on others is crucial to your own success and happiness—then losing a lover is a much greater blow, because not only are you brokenhearted, you also believe you cannot function any more without this other person. When you are complete in yourself, you may hurt when you’ve lost your relationship, but you don’t believe that you’ve lost part of yourself, or something vital to your own conception of yourself.

Question: If you tell a girl about something you’ve done and she said she’s never done it and we should do it sometime, is that implying she wants to hang out?
Answer: No. “We should do that sometime” is not implying anything. It is directly stating in clear language “I want to do $THING with you.” There’s no hint, there’s no implication, it’s a straight-up statement. She is interested in doing the thing with you. If you like the idea of spending time with this person doing this thing, the appropriate response is “That sounds splendid, I’d love to! Got any plans this weekend?”
